Waldorf Astoria Kuala Lumpur opened on 30 October 2026 at 73 Jalan Raja Chulan, in the Golden Triangle of the Malaysian capital. It is the first hotel of Hilton's flagship luxury brand in Malaysia.

## An all-suite hotel

The hotel has 268 suites and no standard rooms. The smallest one-bedroom suites measure 80 m²; the Waldorf Astoria Suite reaches 745 m². The suites were designed by Deboss Collective, and the art collection was curated with the Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia.

General manager Etienne Dalançon, who was previously general manager of Waldorf Astoria Maldives Ithaafushi, leads the hotel. Within Hilton, Asia Pacific is run by Alan Watts, President, Asia Pacific.

## Seven restaurants and bars

Dining is central to the offer. Three concepts carry the name of Jean-Georges Vongerichten: JG KL, abc kitchens KL and The Bar by JG. Yaari, an Indian restaurant, was created with Garima Arora, the Michelin-starred chef of Gaa in Bangkok. The Istana serves breakfast, and Peacock Alley, the brand's signature bar, completes the line-up.

## Spa and events

The Waldorf Astoria Spa covers 2,275 m² over two floors, with seven treatment rooms, alongside a 20-metre outdoor pool. The hotel also offers 3,745 m² of event space, including a 1,545 m² ballroom for up to 2,500 guests.

## Pricing

When La Revue des Hôtels checked on 31 October, a King Deluxe Garden Suite was offered from RM 3,489, about €770, taxes and fees included, for the night of 15 to 16 November 2026. The same suite had been shown at RM 2,094 for January 2027 earlier in October.

## The signal

Kuala Lumpur has long been one of Asia's most affordable luxury capitals. By opening with suites only, Waldorf Astoria sells space rather than a room category, and tests how far the city's price ceiling can rise. Its rates in the coming months will show whether the market follows.
summary: Hilton's flagship luxury brand opened its first Malaysian hotel on 30 October: an all-suite address in the Golden Triangle, with Jean-Georges dining and a 2,275 m² spa.
